en.name: Coagulation factor V antigen
en.shortDescription: Immunological quantity of factor V protein ; distinct from factor V activity (functional)
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context Factor V antigen is the **immunological measurement of the factor V protein concentration** in plasma — what this concept set measures. It quantifies how much factor V protein is present, irrespective of whether the molecule is functionally active [1]. The result is a single numeric value per patient-timestamp, produced on platelet-poor plasma by immunoassay [1, 2]. Results are reported as a percentage of normal plasma concentration — the representation this concept set covers. A separate LOINC code expresses the same assay in IU/mL; it is excluded here because that unit is not convertible to a percentage [3]. **Note: activity vs antigen.** This concept set covers **antigen** only — the immunological mass of the factor V protein. The functional capacity of the protein in the clotting cascade is captured by a separate concept set, "Coagulation factor V activity". The two values can diverge in qualitative deficits where antigen is normal but activity is reduced [1] — they are different study variables and must not be merged. ## Included Concepts The set contains a single LOINC "Lab Test" concept, measuring factor V antigenic concentration in platelet-poor plasma by immunoassay: - *3023945 / 3195-5 — Coagulation factor V Ag actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC)*: result expressed as a **percentage** of pooled normal plasma antigenic concentration. **Note on units.** The recommended unit is **`%`** (OMOP concept 8554 — percent), the proportion of pooled normal plasma antigenic concentration, as listed by LOINC for `3195-5`. Sources reporting factor V antigen in `U/mL` or `IU/mL` are measuring the concentration variant excluded from this set — see *Excluded Concepts* below. ## Excluded Concepts One concept is explicitly excluded by name (see the note on units below). The following LOINC concepts that exist for factor V are also not part of this set: - **Factor V activity** (`3005757 / 3193-0 — Coagulation factor V activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): captured by the separate concept set "Coagulation factor V activity". - **Factor V inhibitor** (`3004057 / 3191-4 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`, `21494686 / 81124-0 — Coagulation factor V inhibitor [Presence] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): rare bleeding disorder workup, separate scope. - **Factor V activity and inhibitor panel** (`36031832 / 96458-5 — Coagulation factor V activity and inhibitor panel - Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay`): panel grouping concept, not a measurement result. **Note on excluded units.** Concept 3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay (LOINC) is excluded from this set. It reports an *activity concentration* in arbitrary units (`[arb'U]/mL`) rather than a proportion of normal plasma, and the two are not interchangeable: UCUM defines arbitrary units as non-dimensional and non-convertible, while IUPAC/IFCC call the same thing a *procedure-defined unit* — a unit whose reference is set by the individual laboratory or measuring device. No conversion factor to `%` can therefore be stated with confidence. In practice laboratories report factor V as a percentage of normal (typically 50–200 % in adults [2]), and no published source documents reference values in `[arb'U]/mL`. Should a data provider actually report this concept, it warrants its own concept set rather than being merged here. ## Mapping Notes - **Default concept** when the source explicitly reports "factor V antigen", "factor V Ag", "facteur V antigène" with the result expressed as a percentage of normal: `3023945 / 3195-5 — Coagulation factor V Ag actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay`. - **Source reports IU/mL or U/mL for factor V antigen**: do **not** map here. That representation corresponds to `3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay`, which is excluded from this set because its arbitrary unit cannot be converted to a percentage of normal. - **Source reports a single "factor V" without specifying activity vs antigen**: by default, map to the "Coagulation factor V activity" concept set — the activity assay is the routine clinical measurement; antigen is a specialty test. Only map to this antigen concept set when the source unambiguously labels the result as "Ag" / "antigen" / "antigène". - **Do not confuse with**: factor V activity (different concept set), factor V Leiden genotype (genetic test, not immunoassay), factor V inhibitor titre. ## References [1] Asselta R, Tenchini ML, Duga S. Inherited defects of coagulation factor V: the hemorrhagic side. *J Thromb Haemost*. 2006;4(1):26-34. Available: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-7836.2005.01590.x [2] Regenstrief Institute. LOINC code 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay. Available: https://loinc.org/3194-8/ [3] Nomenclature for Properties and Units (NPU). IFCC/IUPAC. NPU codes (current release). Available: https://npu-terminology.org/npu-database/

versions.message: Exclude concept 3027396 / 3194-8 — Coagulation factor V Ag [Units/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Immunoassay. It reports an activity concentration in arbitrary units, which UCUM defines as non-convertible and IUPAC/IFCC as a procedure-defined unit, so no reliable equivalence to the actual/normal ratio kept in this set can be stated. Laboratories report factor V as a percentage of normal and no source documents reference values in [arb'U]/mL; if a provider does report this concept, it warrants its own concept set.
